sentences.text: Each bag remains under controlled custody from screening release until an authorized loading handoff is confirmed.
The Baggage Control System maintains the bag identity, assigned flight, screening disposition, and current handling status as the authoritative record.
Staff keep bags in monitored areas and prevent access by personnel who are not assigned to the active handling task.
The Induction Tray Conveyor carries only bags with readable identity data and a valid route assignment into the screening process.
The Primary Crossbelt Sorter directs cleared bags to their assigned make-up destination and diverts unresolved items from normal handling.
The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner must report healthy status before their screening results are relied upon for release.
The Image Resolution Desk reviews images that require operator assessment and records a disposition before the bag can continue.
Any unresolved screening result places the bag in a controlled hold area until the required review is complete.
The Explosives Response Team assesses security events referred for specialist action and communicates the resulting disposition through approved operational channels.
The Secondary Inspection Chute is kept clear of unrelated bags so that identity and custody remain unambiguous during inspection.
The Security Duty Manager uses the seal log to verify that recorded custody seals remain accounted for and that any discrepancy has been escalated.
A Maintenance Technician reports equipment faults that could affect bag identity, screening integrity, or controlled access before the equipment is returned to service.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor confirms that outstanding holds and route exceptions have an assigned owner before authorizing continuation of processing.
Orchard shall release a bag to the next handling stage only when the recorded screening disposition and assigned destination are valid.
The Flight Data Gateway provides the flight and destination data used to check that the bag remains assigned to an operating departure.
The Bag Reconciliation Station compares scanned bag identities against the expected flight population and flags missing or duplicate records for resolution.
The Airline Ramp Coordinator uses the Bag Match Query to review unresolved bag-to-flight mismatches before loading authorization is granted.
The East Make-Up Conveyor moves reconciled bags toward the correct flight position without bypassing required identity checks.
The West Make-Up Conveyor remains subject to the same controlled access and reconciliation rules as other make-up equipment.
The Transfer Bag Feeder accepts transfer bags only when their identity and intended onward flight can be verified.
The Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the flight assignment, reconciled bag count, and operational status are consistent before accepting the loading record.
Before aircraft loading, the Airline Ramp Coordinator verifies that the bag identity is readable, the flight assignment is current, and the security disposition permits loading.
The physical bags presented for loading must agree with the reconciled records, and every unexplained count or identity difference blocks acceptance.
A bag is ready for departure only after screening release, custody continuity, final reconciliation, and loading checks are all complete and recorded.
